title: Serving runtime weekly update - kernel / KV cache / batching (2026-09-02)
body:
TL;DR:
- Kernel microkernels PR (#432) landed in feature branch; initial canary shows ~12% lower decode CPU time for medium-length chat workloads.
- KV cache memory compaction landed behind a flag; mem usage down ~22% at 99th percentile for long-context sessions.
- Dynamic batching heuristic adjusted to use sequence-length stratification (short/medium/long) — throughput up 8% overall, p99 latency improved for medium requests.

Highlights / Notes:
- Kernel work (Amit + Priya):
  - PR 432 implements fused attention write-path and a faster rotary embedding inner loop optimized for Ampere/next-gen kernels. Benchmarks on internal perf harness (A100 fleet) show average decode step time reduced by 12% on 8K-token horizon with the medium-profile model.
  - Still flaky on older drivers (driver 470.*) — we have a compatibility shim that falls back to old kernels; need QA sign-off before enabling cluster-wide.
  - Next: land CI perf tests (microbench + end-to-end) and open canary to 5% of hosted traffic.

- KV cache (Diego + Laura):
  - Implemented in-memory compaction + segmented LRU evictions. When compaction flag is on, per-session KV memory drops ~22% in long-tail workloads (sessions > 6k tokens). This reduces OOM incidents seen during multi-tenant stress tests.
  - Added serialization format v2 (smaller, faster deserialize). Backwards-compatible; we need migration plan for Dedicated clusters.
  - Observed a 0.5% increase in p50 latency for cache-miss cases due to compaction overhead; profiling shows lock contention spikes that we'll optimize next week.

- Batching (Priya + team):
  - Deployed stratified dynamic batching: requests binned by length percentile and then batched up to configurable per-bin max_batch. This prevents long tails in mixed-length batches that previously caused p99 tail latency.
  - In canary on staging, stratified batching increased aggregate throughput by ~8% and reduced p99 generation latency by ~18% for mixed workloads.
  - Investigating combined effect of batch-size auto-scaling and kernel selection (microkernel chooses an optimized path for batches >= 16).

Performance metrics (staging canary results, week-over-week):
- Decode step time (median) for medium-profile model: 42ms -> 37ms (12% improvement)
- 95th generation token latency (mixed workloads): 420ms -> 345ms (18% improvement)
- KV memory per-session 99th: 1.8GB -> 1.4GB (22% reduction)
- CPU utilization (serving nodes): ~+3% (acceptable tradeoff for performance)

Incidents / Reliability:
- 2026-08-29: One Dedicated customer reported elevated OOMs during a long-context stress run. Root cause: older KV serialization format + no compaction enabled. Fix: compaction flag enabled and migration doc created for Dedicated. Customer remediation: hotfix + restart window; monitoring confirmed stabilization.

Open blockers / Risks:
- Driver compatibility for new kernels (older driver versions trigger fallback) — needs SRE coordination to ensure fallback paths are robust.
- Dedicated rollout: serialization v2 migration needs automated migration tooling to avoid long restarts for customers with thousands of sessions.
- Lock contention in KV compaction path impacting some cache-miss latencies — profiling and lock-free structure proposals due next week.

Meetings / Decisions this week:
- 2026-09-01 Kernel sync: decided to gate kernel rollout behind canary + driver-version check; rollback plan documented in PR 432.
- 2026-09-02 Ops sync: Dedicated rollout to be staged per-customer with migration playbook; Priya to lead customer comms for first five customers.

Action items (owner - due):
- Amit: Finish CI perf tests and merge perf CI into mainline (due 2026-09-07) — blocked on infra test flakiness.
- Priya: Draft Dedicated migration playbook for serialization v2 and schedule dry-run with 2 pilot customers (due 2026-09-10).
- Diego: Optimize KV compaction lock; propose lock-free ring buffer approach and run microbench (due 2026-09-09).
- Laura: Run 48-hour canary with kernel flag enabled on 5% hosted traffic and collect perf+error telemetry (start 2026-09-03).
- SRE (assigned): Validate driver-version distribution across clusters and produce a compatibility matrix (due 2026-09-08).

Notes / Misc:
- Link to perf dashboards: https://console.redwood.ai/perf/serving-runtime (internal) — updated charts for kernel branch and canary cohorts.
- Remember to include a rollback tag in PRs touching runtime entrypoints.
- Suggestion from infra: add a per-session KV soft-limit that triggers background compaction earlier to avoid compaction spikes during hot path handling.

Observations / informal:
- Team sentiment: optimistic — visible wins from kernel work but a few infra-level integration tasks remain.
- Need to keep docs up-to-date for Dedicated customers; the migration/messaging work will take ~2 engineer-weeks across eng + solutions.

Next week plan (high level):
- Kernel: CI perf + canary, finalize rollback scripts.
- KV: lock contention fix + extended canary.
- Batching: integrate kernel batch-size heuristics and run end-to-end load tests.

If anything should be prioritized differently, reply here or tag in Slack (#eng-serving-runtime).

-- Maria
